digest.component_or_area: Lock management for enrichment drain, compaction worker, and GC trigger
propositions: Three nearly identical O_EXCL lock-acquisition loops exist across enrich_drain, compact_trigger, and gc_trigger, each wrapping os.open with stamped_file_is_stale reclamation

The drain's release implementation wraps close+unlink in a single try-block, causing unlink to be skipped if close raises, leaking the lock until the 3600s ceiling; the other two use independent try-blocks
The drain appends newline to the stamp bytes while compaction and GC do not; both readers strip() so the difference is invisible but should be normalized
The stamp-failure handling differs: the drain warns explicitly while others swallow the error silently; the shared implementation must adopt the drain's warning everywhere
Directory creation mechanisms differ across all three workers and must remain with callers; the shared lock helper takes a resolved path and owns no directory creation

Consolidating the three copies into a single stamped_lock module with two functions—acquire and release—eliminates duplication while fixing the drain's release-on-close-failure bug and establishing uniform logging
